question: Junito’ is the nickname of ***which four-weight world champion boxer*** who lost via unanimous decision to Floyd Mayweather in 2012? He represented Puerto Rico at the Olympics in Sydney.
American band the Mooney Suzuki named themselves after two of the lead vocalists of ***which German experimental rock group*** that was particularly active in the late 1960s and early 1970s?
Salix alba is the scientific name for the white species of ***what genus of tree***? Salicylic acid, a precursor to aspirin, was first derived from the bark of this tree.
Kippers are a dish consisting of smoked fillets of ***which fish***?
The death of ***which English King*** in January 1066 led to a protracted battle for the throne during that year? He was the brother-in-law of his successor Harold Godwinson.
Celebrating the patron saint of Wales, Saint David’s Day is the first day of ***which month***?
The US state Louisiana uses ***what term*** to refer to its subdivisions instead of counties? This term is also used for the main subdivisions of Jamaica.

Zeno of Citium was the founder of ***which school of philosophy*** that emphasised adherence to the four cardinal virtues and detachment from worldly emotions? This school of philosophy gives its name to a word used to describe people who do not complain about suffering.
Norwegian king Harald Hardrada was killed at ***which battle of September 1066***? This battle took place in Yorkshire and shares its name with that of a Premier League football ground.
Celebrating the patron saint of Scotland, Saint Andrew’s Day is the final day of ***which month***?
***Which city on the Silk Road*** was burned down by Genghis Khan in 1220, but later became the centre of the Timurid dynasty? It is the location of the Mausoleum of Timur.
Acting as regent for her son from 267 CE, which ***third-century Queen*** of the Palmyrene Empire annexed Egypt and Anatolia but was deposed in 272 after declaring independence from the Romans?
A highly-toxic tetra⸱ethyl derivative of ***which heavy metal*** was used as an anti-knocking agent in petrol before being phased out of automotive fuels in the early 2000s?
In the sit-com 'Allo 'Allo, ***what is René’s call sign*** when communicating with London?

Not to be confused with the capital of  Saint Kitts, Basse-Terre, located on an island of the same name, is the capital city of ***which French overseas department*** that forms part of the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean?
Bondi Beach is located around 7 kilometres from the centre of ***which Australian city***?
***Which Pink Floyd album***, best known for its acoustic title song and the epic ‘Shine On You Crazy Diamond’, celebrates the 50th anniversary of its release in 2025?
In January 2025, Timothée Chalamet was nominated for a Golden Globe acting award for his role as Bob Dylan in ***which biographical film***?

***What was the surname*** of the husband-and-wife astronomers with the forenames Carolyn and Eugene who co-discovered a comet in 1993 with David Levy? The comet crashed into Jupiter in 1994, producing the first directly observable extraterrestrial collision of Solar System objects.
***What drinks brand*** sponsored the ride the Big One at Blackpool Pleasure Beach until 2011? From 1994 to 1996 this was the tallest rollercoaster in the world.
In July 2024, Jessica Campbell became the first female coach of an NHL team when she was hired as assistant coach for ***what franchise***, who play in Seattle and joined the league in 2021?
***What diss track***, targeted at Drake, won Kendrick Lamar five awards at the 2025 Grammys, including Record of the Year and Song of the Year?

Effectively the opposite of a ristretto, ***what is the name of the Italian coffee drink*** that uses twice as much water as an espresso shot? It is similar to an americano, except that all the water is brewed.
The spice vanilla is obtained from pods from ***which family of flowering plants***, which also includes a subfamily commonly known by the term ‘slipper’?
In January 2025, Robbie Williams was a co-nominee for a Golden Globe for Best Original Song for ‘Forbidden Road’ taken from ***which film*** about Williams’s early life?
A 1786 opera by Mozart tells the story of Susanna’s marriage to ***what title character***?
Also celebrating its 50th anniversary this year is ***which classic album by Led Zeppelin***, which includes fan favourites ‘Trampled Under Foot’ and ‘Kashmir’?
***Which painting***, usually attributed to Leonardo da Vinci, became the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction when it fetched over $450 million in 2017?
*If you see me walking down the street* is the opening line of ***which 2001 song***, the first UK number one and biggest-selling single for Atomic Kitten?

***Which American rapper*** was nominated for eight awards at the 2025 Grammys, including for his appearance alongside Taylor Swift on the song ‘Fortnight’? He now has received 18 nominations without a win, a record for a musician.
‘The Road Not Taken’ is a 1915 poem by ***which American poet***?
Roxie Hart is the lead character in ***which Kander & Ebb musical***, set in the USA during the Jazz Age?
***What is the Italian word*** for ‘ham’? In English it typically refers to uncooked, unsmoked and dry-cured ham, and it represents winter on a four seasons pizza alongside olives.
Witches’ Sabbath and Saturn Devouring His Son, both likely completed at some point between 1820 and 1823, are notable works in the so-called series of ‘Black Paintings’ by ***which Spanish artist***?
***Which electronic music group*** released the 2011 album Welcome Reality? Singles from that album included ‘Guilt’, ‘Me and You’, and ‘Promises’.
***What name*** is given to the stew used by sumo wrestlers as part of their weight-gain diet?

A colloid is a mixture in which particles of one substance are suspended throughout another substance. ***What name*** is given to a colloid consisting of a liquid dispersed in another liquid? Common examples include mayonnaise, hand creams, and certain paints.
***Who*** was the commander of HMS Bounty at the time of the famous mutiny in 1789?
***Which American golfer*** won his fifth major title at the 2023 PGA Championship? In doing so, he became the first golfer on the LIV tour to win a major championship.

***Which country*** narrowly missed out on becoming the first African team to reach the semi finals of the FIFA World Cup in 2010 when Luis Suárez famously stopped a last-minute winner from being scored by handling the ball on the goal line in their quarter final match? Uruguay then went on to win the match on penalties.
***Which French mathematician*** gives his name to the fundamental theorem that allows the reduction of certain problems in field theory to group theory?
The city of Manchester is fictionalised as Coketown in ***which novel by Charles Dickens***, that features the characters Josiah Bounderby and Mr Gradgrind?

***What Pacific island nation*** was given the name New Hebrides when it was explored by Captain Cook in 1774 and retained that name until independence? Cook gave the islands this name as, like nearby New Caledonia, they reminded him of Scotland.
***What type of traditional Russian winter footwear***, taken from the Russian for ‘made by felting’, is commonly worn in extremely cold climates for traversing dry snow?
***Which species of cat*** is the only living member of the Panthera genus that is native to the Americas?
***Which British distance runner***, who won the BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2002, still holds the women’s record for the London Marathon, which has stood since 2003?
The eighth installment of ***which combat arcade game***, developed and published by Bandai Namco, was released in 2024? Its one-word name comes from the Japanese for ‘iron fist’.

***What name*** is given to a contrapuntal classical music composition that employs a melody with at least one imitation of that melody which follows after a rest? Johann Pachelbel wrote a famous example in the key of D.
Taking its name from the Japanese word for ‘fussy’, ***what successful chain of high street restaurants*** serves a range of Asian inspired dishes such as ramen, katsu curry and a firecracker curry?
***What name*** is given to a colloid consisting of either a liquid or solid suspended in a gas? Common examples include mist, smoke and spray paints.
